title: You remember the image.
subtitle: You don't remember the filename.
narration: You remember seeing the image, but not what you named it. Maybe it was an error, a lecture slide, or a receipt. SightVault turns that vague memory into a search.

title: A useful memory for your images
subtitle: Choose a folder. Search what you remember.
cue: A working local prototype · 62-image demo collection
narration: SightVault is a private visual memory for your computer. Choose an image folder, and it builds a searchable local collection. Here, we are using sixty two sample images to show the complete workflow.

title: 01 / Find it by meaning
subtitle: “GPU memory problem” → the actual screenshot
cue: Visual meaning · Direct image and text embeddings
narration: I remember a graphics card memory problem, so I search for GPU memory problem. Visual meaning finds the actual error screenshot, even though those exact words are not the text on screen. Images go directly into the embedding model.

title: 02 / Recover the exact evidence
subtitle: Search an error code. Inspect the original image and OCR.
cue: Hybrid retrieval · OCR text stays attached to its source
narration: When I remember an exact detail, I can search for E resolve. Hybrid search combines visual meaning with extracted text. Opening the result shows the source image and its OCR transcription, so I can check the evidence instead of trusting a generated summary.

title: 03 / Find the earliest indexed match
subtitle: File chronology, with a clear source timestamp
cue: Demo screenshot dates are synthetic · Not proven event history
narration: Next, I search for the CUDA memory error and choose First occurrence. SightVault finds the earliest matching file across the index. These demo screenshot dates are synthetic. This is file chronology, not a claim about when the real event happened.

title: 04 / Ask about what is visible
subtitle: Local image reasoning, beside the source evidence
cue: MiniCPM-V · Visible facts and likely explanations stay distinct
narration: Now I ask what probably caused the error. A local vision model reads the image on demand. Its answer stays beside the screenshot and source reference. It identifies the visible memory shortage and offers a likely explanation, while making clear that a hypothesis is not a proven cause.

title: 05 / Search beyond readable text
subtitle: Find a red backpack, even without a text label
cue: Direct visual retrieval · Red versus blue object discrimination
narration: This is not limited to screenshots with text. Searching for a red backpack finds the illustration itself, with the blue backpack as a nearby alternative. That is direct visual retrieval, rather than a database of generated captions.

title: Your collection stays on your computer
subtitle: Local models. Local storage. Inspectable evidence.
narration: The prototype runs on this Mac. Embedding Gemma creates the image and query vectors. Mini C P M handles OCR and image analysis, with a labeled local OCR fallback. After setup, inference uses local model files, with no cloud model calls.

title: Built. Tested. Demonstrated.
subtitle: A native Apple Silicon prototype with real model inference
cue: 123 tests passed · 17/17 retrieval cases · 30 browser checks
narration: We have a working native Mac prototype, not just a mockup. Validation includes one hundred twenty three passing tests, seventeen successful demo retrieval cases, browser checks, and real model recovery tests. The demo you have seen uses the running app.

title: Less searching. More remembering.
subtitle: SightVault
cue: Next: PDF imports · Smarter collections · Faster bulk indexing
narration: Our next steps are simpler document imports, smarter collections, and faster bulk indexing. For students, developers, and anyone with a growing screenshot folder, SightVault makes saved images useful again. Remember what you saw. Find the evidence. Keep it local.
